messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type:
• 55 mph on rural interstates,
• 65 mph on urban interstates,
• 45 mph on most rural highways,
• 35 mph on many city streets. | Drivers must obey posted signs; no “default” speed limit. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• The law applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles (helmet required). | Failure can result in a $50 fine and points on the driver’s record. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use is prohibited while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Violations carry a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” policy for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• Stop signs and yield signs must be obeyed. | Failure to yield can lead to points and fines. | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during any weather that reduces visibility.
• Fog lights are allowed only when visibility is less than 200 ft. | Failure to use headlights can result in a $25 fine. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing a vehicle requires a valid towing permit if the vehicle is not registered. | Unregistered vehicles can be impounded. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | Violations can lead to towing. | | **School Bus** | • All vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading or unloading children.
• The bus must display its stop sign and flashing lights. | Failure to stop can result in a $500 fine and points. | | **Points System** | • Texas uses a points system for traffic violations.
• Accumulating 12 points in 3 years can lead to license suspension. | Points vary by offense (e.g., 1 point for speeding, 2 for DUI). | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Speed cameras and red‑light cameras are used in many cities.
• Violations are mailed to the registered owner. | Fines are typically higher than manual citations. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles require a helmet.
• Commercial vehicles must follow specific weight and safety regulations. | Commercial drivers face stricter penalties for violations. | ### Quick Reference - **Speed Limit Signs**: Always obey posted signs; no “default” speed limit. - **Seat Belt**: Mandatory for all occupants. - **Cell Phone**: Hand‑held use prohibited; hands‑free allowed. - **DUI**: BAC ≥ 0.08 % (lower for commercial/under‑21). - **Right‑of‑Way**: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles on the right at uncontrolled intersections. - **Headlights**: On from sunset to sunrise or when visibility is reduced. - **Parking**: No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks; handicap spaces require permits. - **School Bus**: Stop for loading/unloading children. - **Points**: 12 points in 3 years can suspend your license. For the most up‑to‑date and detailed information, consult the Texas Department of Public Safety website or the Texas Transportation Code.
